title: Why the King Walks Slowly
body: Have you ever wondered why the chess king only moves one square at a time? King Alfonso of Spain wrote that a real leader must never rush blindly into battle, but should instead step carefully while watching over his army.

variants.lucy: Long ago, a wise Spanish ruler named King Alfonso explained why our chess king takes such tiny, quiet steps. He believed that a true leader never runs in a hurry or panics. Instead, the king walks slowly to look closely at each of his brave soldiers and keep them safe.
variants.luca: You might think a king should charge ahead on a fast horse, but an old Spanish ruler named Alfonso had a far better plan. He wrote that a great commander must never sprint into a trap. By moving just one square at a time, the leader can scout the battlefield and guide his whole army to victory.
variants.cn: 很久以前，西班牙聪明的国王阿方索解释过，为什么棋盘上的王每次只迈小小的、安安静静的一步。他觉得，一位真正的首领从不慌慌张张地乱跑。王慢慢地走，是为了把每一个勇敢的士兵都看仔细，护他们周全。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón
